name: 4-bit ALU
description: Small combinational 4-bit ALU (ADD, SUB, AND, OR) with carry and zero flags, verified by an exhaustive self-checking testbench (all 1024 input combinations) with functional coverage and two injectable bugs.
spec: Design a purely combinational 4-bit ALU named alu4 (no clock, no reset, no latches). Inputs: a[3:0], b[3:0], op[1:0]. Outputs: y[3:0], carry, zero. op 00 ADD: {carry, y} = a + b (carry is the carry out of the 5-bit sum). op 01 SUB: y = a - b computed as a + ~b + 1; carry is the carry out of that sum, so carry = 1 means no borrow (a >= b as unsigned numbers) and carry = 0 means a borrow occurred. op 10 AND: y = a & b, carry = 0. op 11 OR: y = a | b, carry = 0. zero = 1 exactly when y == 0.

bugs.title: SUB computes b - a
bugs.description: The operands of the subtract path are swapped (b + ~a + 1), so SUB returns b - a. Only a == b survives: y is wrong whenever a - b is not 0 or 8 (mod 16), and carry is inverted for every a != b because the no-borrow test effectively becomes b >= a. ADD, AND and OR are unaffected.

bugs.title: Zero flag ignores y[3]
bugs.description: The zero detector only compares y[2:0] (a width slip left over from a 3-bit version of the ALU), so a result of 4'b1000 is flagged as zero. Every other result is correct, so only the vectors whose result is exactly 0x8 fail - the kind of bug that slips through a handful of directed tests but not an exhaustive sweep.
